The world's tallest building stands on sand? 🏜️ Watch the Burj Khalifa go up: 6 years in 30 seconds. ⏱️

Test holes found no hard bedrock, so it stands on 192 concrete piles, 1.5 m wide and over 50 m deep, under a 3.7 m concrete mat. Then a Y-shaped core rose floor after floor, with concrete pumped a record 606 m up, often poured at night to stay cool. Over 26,000 glass panels. 27 setbacks to confuse the wind.

The twist: the 200 m+ spire was built inside the tower, then jacked up into place.

Would you work at 800 m? Yes or no 👇

Next: the Statue of Liberty. Follow so you don't miss it.

yt_title: How the Burj Khalifa Was Built: 6 Years in 30 Seconds #shorts
yt_description:
No hard bedrock: 192 bored piles (1.5 m, 50 m+ deep) under a 3.7 m concrete mat, a Y-shaped buttressed core, concrete pumped a record 606 m, 26,000+ glass panels, 27 spiral setbacks, and a 200 m+ steel spire built inside the tower and jacked up. 2004–2010, 828 m.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burj_Khalifa · https://www.burjkhalifa.ae/en/the-tower/structures/
Figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
